Tom — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery: 

- Primary workload: product search & summarization for end-user queries (mix of short & medium context).
- Expected production volume: ~50M tokens/month to start, scaling to 150-200M tokens/month in 9–12 months depending on adoption.
- Performance targets: p95 latency <250ms for 1–2 concurrent requests; throughput ~200 reqs/s at peak.
- Security: VPC option + KMS required for initial pilot.

Pricing / budget: you mentioned a target unit economics goal — internal leadership is looking for guidance on a target $/1M tokens that would make this work against your retention model. If you can confirm a target range that would be a win (e.g., $X–$Y per 1M tokens), we can run a tighter multi-model cost comparison and proposed configuration (dedicated vs hosted).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm target $/1M tokens and any firm budget ceilings.
2) Share a short sample of real traffic patterns (tokens per request distribution) if possible — helps optimize batching/quantization recommendations.
3) I’ll send a short benchmark comparing Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic/open-model hosts for the mix you described + a pricing breakdown (will share CSV & PDF).

Attaching a draft benchmark template — I’ll populate with Redwood numbers and obvious public/market comps, but would love to validate your target price so our recommendation aligns.

Best,

Subject: Pricing benchmark (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosts) + next steps

Tom — thanks for the clarification and the target ranges — that’s exactly the detail we needed. I’ve run an initial model-level unit economics sketch (attached CSV + PDF). High-level findings below (assumptions: mixed model strategy — open models for high-volume retrieval/recap; higher-capacity models for critical summarization flows):

- Acme target: $20–$30 / 1M tokens (bulk open-model usage) — we can be competitive in that range with Redwood Dedicated + quantized open models for the bulk path.
- Higher-quality path (few-shot summarization): up to $60 / 1M tokens — Redwood can meet parity with public LLM APIs depending on model choice; for gpt-4-class workloads OpenAI list pricing is materially higher.
- Market comps (illustrative):
  - OpenAI (GPT-4/GPT-4o style): ~$60–$200 / 1M tokens depending on context & variant (higher for larger context),
  - OpenAI (GPT-3.5/mid-tier): ~$6–$12 / 1M tokens,
  - Anthropic (Claude-class): ~$30–$80 / 1M tokens (varies by model),
  - Open-model hosts/self-hosted (quantized 8-bit variants): ~$10–$30 / 1M tokens (depends on utilization and batching).

Key levers that move unit economics: batching rate, KV/prefix caching, sequence length distribution, quantization level, and reserved capacity pricing. For your volume profile (~100M pilot) a Dedicated pool with aggressive batching + 8-bit quantization on the retrieval path typically reduces unit cost 2–4x vs naive hosted configurations.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You share the anonymized token-size distribution (even a simple histogram) — we’ll re-run the CSV with exact batching/throughput assumptions.
2) I’ll loop in Marissa (cc’d) to run a Dedicated pool TCO for 100M & 200M token scenarios and produce a recommended $/1M target with explicit breakdown (compute, infra, ops, margin).
3) If that looks reasonable we can put together a pilot SOW for Private deployment (VPC + KMS).

I’ve attached the working benchmark: ACME_Multi-Model_Benchmark.csv (columns: model, tokens_per_call_avg, latency_ms_p95, cost_per_1M_est_redwood, cost_per_1M_public_comp). Also attached Redwood_pricing_breakdown_v2.pdf with a human-readable sketch.

Would you be available Tue or Wed next week for a 30-min follow-up to review the numbers?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
